s2.p1: No WDSF member federation: Oceania’s only two are **Australia** and **New Zealand**. We found no ballroom school or competition in Fiji.
s2.p2: What we found: a ==Salsa and Tango night== at the Royal Suva Yacht Club in July 2025, and a **Brazilian zouk** social in Suva in June 2026.

s3.p: performed at **Dance Fest Fiji 2025**, two from New Zealand and Australia: the largest line-up since it began in 2020. Styles: **contemporary, island, hip-hop**.

s4.p1: A Bauan **war dance**, sung to inspire warriors and on their victorious return. In 1939, captain Ratu Sir George Cakobau wanted an answer to the **haka**.
s4.p2: For Fiji’s tour of New Zealand, Ratu Bola, of Bau’s warrior clan, taught it to the team. They stayed ==unbeaten==: 7 wins, 1 draw.

s5.name: SEASEA
s5.p: Called the most graceful meke. The feet barely move: the action is in the **iri ni meke**, a woven pandanus fan, and in the head and upper body.

s5.name: LAHANGA
s5.p: An **Indo-Fijian** dance by a male performer in a long layered skirt, its top layer swayed by hand. Traditionally seen at **weddings and religious festivals**.

s6.p: In Rukua village, a historian told how the **daunivucu** (composer) received meke lyrics ==in dreams==, 3 or 4 verses at a time. 30 verses took **about 10 days**.

s7.p: The **Leonidas** reached Levuka on 14 May with the first indentured labourers from India. By 1916, **60,553** had arrived. 14 May is now **Girmit Day**.
s7.p2: VOU’s **Fijian Flying Circus** tours Darwin, Brisbane, Melbourne and Sydney, ==Aug 2026 to Jan 2027==, after headlining New Zealand’s Hamilton Arts Festival in February.
